propositions: acli_graph.py hand-rolls three identical cursor-pagination loops with no runaway-token guard, creating infinite-loop risk when a server repeats the same nextPageToken
A server returning the same non-null nextPageToken consecutively causes silent silent-partial degradation because the fail-open exception handler at each map swallows the runaway condition
Shared _iter_cursor_pages iterator with RunawayPaginationError must escape the fail-open handlers (except RunawayPaginationError: raise ahead of catch-all) to preserve data-integrity signal
All three acli_graph maps rewired to consume the shared cursor iterator instead of hand-rolling loops, eliminating code duplication and centralizing the runaway guard
Structural tests updated to pin iterator wiring and verify runaway-token conditions propagate as exceptions rather than returning partial dicts
